interpretations: For each college, sum income.amount over incomes joined income → member (link_to_member) → major (link_to_major); the fraction is that college's sum divided by the total of income.amount across all income records, including incomes with no member or major.
Same college totals, but the fraction's denominator is the total income only for the incomes that link to a member with a major, so the fractions sum to 1.
Same as interpretation 1, but the fraction is expressed as a percentage (multiplied by 100) rather than a decimal fraction.

Same as interpretation 1, but the denominator is the sum of income.amount across all income records in the income table, computed with integer division (no decimals) versus real-number division, so "without rounding" means avoiding integer truncation.
"Without rounding" means returning the raw, unrounded fraction value, with no ROUND function applied.
Colleges are grouped by major.college name, so majors from different departments in the same college are combined into one row.
Colleges are grouped by college, but each distinct (college, department) or major is separated, so the same college appears more than once.
Only colleges that have at least one linked income record are shown (inner joins).
All colleges in the major table are shown, including those with no income (total 0, fraction 0), via left joins from major.
The total income amount is the sum of income.amount, counting each income record once.
The total income amount is the sum of income.amount after joining through attendance or other tables, which could duplicate records. (Unlikely, since the question links only via the member.)
"The member who brought it in" is interpreted as income.link_to_member (the member who received or contributed the funds).
The fraction is the college's total divided by the grand total of all income, as a single number per college.
The output has three columns: college, total income amount, and fraction.
The output has only college and fraction, with the total amount implied.
queries:
SELECT ma.college, CAST(SUM(i.amount) AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(amount) FROM income) AS fraction
FROM income i
JOIN member m ON i.link_to_member = m.member_id
JOIN major ma ON m.link_to_major = ma.major_id
GROUP BY ma.college

SELECT ma.college, SUM(i.amount) AS total_income, SUM(i.amount) * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(i2.amount) FROM income i2 JOIN member m2 ON i2.link_to_member = m2.member_id JOIN major ma2 ON m2.link_to_major = ma2.major_id) AS fraction
FROM income i
JOIN member m ON i.link_to_member = m.member_id
JOIN major ma ON m.link_to_major = ma.major_id
GROUP BY ma.college
SELECT (SELECT SUM(spent) FROM budget) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(amount) FROM income) AS percentage;
SELECT major.college, COUNT(member.member_id) FROM member JOIN major ON member.link_to_major = major.major_id GROUP BY major.college;
